models.name: Yaob Next
models.summary: A locally runnable AI system combining a 4-billion-parameter cognitive core with a persistent knowledge network containing more than 10,000 nodes.
models.licence: Free to use and share, not to sell. Qwen models: Apache-2.0. Network: CC BY-SA 4.0 and CC0. Router: source-available, no resale
models.install_md:
Yaob Next is one file. MPN Studio runs it on your computer, offline.

1. Install [MPN Studio 0.2.0](https://github.com/sarja-technologies/mpn-studio/releases/tag/v0.2.0) for your computer (x86-64 or ARM64). On Ubuntu or Debian: `sudo apt install ./mpn-studio_0.2.0_amd64.deb` (`arm64` on ARM64).
2. Download `Yaob-Next-N10K-C4B-0.2.0.mpn` and check it:

   ```
   echo "67e56f1e4a6cbabdc6414d25de6f80272a811c17ca1ffb6cb045301760efd53c  Yaob-Next-N10K-C4B-0.2.0.mpn" | sha256sum -c
   ```

3. Open MPN Studio, choose **Models**, then **Open .mpn file**, and pick the file. (With the .deb installed, double-clicking the file also opens it.)
4. Open the model and press **Start** in its chat panel. The first start unpacks the file (6.2 GiB) before the model loads. Then ask a question: the answer lists the nodes it used.

In a terminal instead: `mpn run Yaob-Next-N10K-C4B-0.2.0.mpn --chat`. `mpn verify` checks every part of the file.

models.name: Yaob N10K
models.summary: A learned router chooses which of 10,000 knowledge nodes a question needs, and a frozen 4-billion-parameter core answers from their text. Most of the accuracy comes from that retrieval.
models.licence: Code and weights: source-available, no resale. Node data: CC BY-SA 4.0. Base models: Apache-2.0
models.install_md:
Yaob comes as its source code plus eight model files. A script downloads the files, checks every checksum and puts the core back together.

1. Get the code. You need Python 3.12 or newer.

   ```
   git clone https://github.com/sarja-technologies/yaob
   cd yaob
   python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
   pip install -e '.[model]'
   ```

2. Download and check the model files (9.3 GB):

   ```
   scripts/fetch_release.sh ~/yaob
   ```

3. Import the network and start Yaob. The [install guide](https://github.com/sarja-technologies/yaob/blob/main/docs/install.md) has the two commands, and how to ask questions from the command line or any OpenAI-compatible app.

   On a 12 GB graphics card, run `mpn budget set context_tokens=4096`, so a long request is refused instead of running out of memory. With less than 32 GB of system memory, also run `mpn budget set reserve_gib=4`: by default Yaob keeps 16 GiB free for other programs and refuses requests that would cut into it.

mpns.name: Yaob N10K
mpns.summary: The original Yaob N10K network: 10,000 nodes in use (9,808 knowledge and 192 procedure) and 105,857 relationships, plus 160 invented diagnostic canary nodes. Provided as a read-only FG-MPN store and as an MPN Studio store, with its trained router; there is no language model in it.
mpns.licence: CC-BY-SA-4.0: Network data (store/, modules.json, studio/network/yaob-n10k.sqlite): CC-BY-SA-4.0, Wikidata facts CC0-1.0 on their own; per-record licences in ATTRIBUTION.md. studio/network/checkpoint/ (router weights, files with licence LicenseRef-Fylume-Source-Available-1.0-Weights): Fylume Source-Available Terms 1.0 for weights, text in studio/network/checkpoint/LICENSE-ROUTER (not CC-BY-SA)
mpns.install_md:
1. Download the repository at this revision from Hugging Face and check it: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`.
2. FG-MPN store, read-only (needs the `fgmpn` 0.2.2 runtime, a private preview): `fgmpn install store ~/mpn/yaob-n10k`, then `fgmpn verify ~/mpn/yaob-n10k`.
3. Studio store, with MPN Studio 0.2.0 or later: `mpn-studio mpn network import-yaob studio "Yaob N10K"`. It imports the network with its router; a core and the encoder are needed to answer questions. No released MPN Studio reads the FG-MPN store.

mpns.summary: Yaob Next N10K is the same network as Yaob N10K 0.1.0 at a later revision: 7 more nodes, 31 more relationships and three nodes edited. apps.name: MPN Studio
apps.summary: The Linux desktop application for creating, opening, editing, versioning and exporting Modular Persistent Network projects and models.
apps.install_md:
MPN Studio is a desktop application. It needs no Python, Node.js or internet connection.

1. Download the package and `SHA256SUMS-x86_64` from the release page, then check the download:

   ```
   sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS-x86_64 --ignore-missing
   ```

2. On Ubuntu or Debian, install the package and start **MPN Studio** from the menu, or run `mpn-studio`:

   ```
   sudo apt install ./mpn-studio_0.4.1_amd64.deb
   ```

   On other Linux systems, run the AppImage:

   ```
   chmod +x MPN-Studio_0.4.1_x86_64.AppImage && ./MPN-Studio_0.4.1_x86_64.AppImage
   ```

3. Choose **Create project** for a blank project, or **Open project** for a project folder, a `.mpn` model or a large network.

cores.name: Qwen3.5-4B Q8_0 GGUF (Yaob core)
cores.summary: Alibaba Cloud's Qwen3.5-4B converted to GGUF and quantised to Q8_0, with its F16 vision projector: the cognitive core of Yaob Next. This is not a Fylume model: Fylume did not fine-tune, merge or otherwise change the weights.
cores.licence: Apache-2.0: Alibaba Cloud's Qwen3.5-4B, converted and quantised only; LICENSE and NOTICE (statement of change) travel with the files

core.name: Qwen3.5-4B Q8_0 GGUF (Yaob core)
core.architecture: qwen35 (hybrid linear/full attention, 33 blocks incl. 1 next-token-prediction block) with a qwen3vl_merger vision projector; language model 4,326,350,848 parameters, projector 333,514,240

cores.name: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B F16 GGUF (Yaob encoder)
cores.summary: Alibaba Cloud's Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B converted to GGUF at F16: the frozen encoder that Yaob's learned router was trained against. This is not a Fylume model, and Fylume did not fine-tune it.
cores.licence: Apache-2.0: Alibaba Cloud's Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (Apache-2.0 declared in the model card; upstream repository has no LICENSE file), converted only

core.name: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B F16 GGUF (Yaob encoder)
core.architecture: qwen3 embedding model (28 blocks, width 1024, last-token pooling, 1024-d vectors)

cores.name: Yaob N10K specialist adapters 0.1.0 (experimental)
cores.summary: Four experimental LoRA adapters (astronomy, chemistry, history and a diagnostic canary module) that Fylume trained for Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, the core of Yaob N10K 0.1.0. They are off by default in Yaob, made declining questions about invented entities worse, and do not work with Qwen3.5-4B.
cores.licence: LicenseRef-Fylume-Source-Available-1.0-Weights: Apache-2.0 text plus Fylume No-Resale Condition 1.0 for weights; not open source. Section 7: astronomy, chemistry and history adapters were trained on CC BY-SA 4.0 Wikipedia text and fall back to CC BY-SA 4.0 where they are adapted material; the diagnostic-canary adapter was trained on text invented by Fylume

core.name: Yaob N10K specialist adapters 0.1.0 (experimental)
core.architecture: LoRA rank 16 alpha 32 on all linear projections of Qwen3ForCausalLM (36 layers); 4 adapters of 33,030,144 parameters
